reviews.rationale: Tm7sf2 knockout mice show hepatic lipid accumulation, ER stress and delayed cell-cycle progression in regenerating liver, confirming its enzymatic role in hepatic sterol biosynthesis. Directly matches mechanism 1's claim about TM7SF2 hepatocyte function.

evidence_span.text: Acyl-CoA synthetase short chain family member 2 (ACSS2), which converts acetate into acetyl-CoA, was notably upregulated in fructose-consuming LAKO mice

reviews.rationale: Hepatic Acss2 knockdown strongly suppressed fructose-derived fatty acid synthesis, establishing it as the key enzyme converting acetate to acetyl-CoA for hepatic lipogenesis, matching the mechanism's claim.

reviews.rationale: Patient genotyping links MVD/PMVK loss-of-function mutations to porokeratosis, and their disease-related phenotype responds to cholesterol replenishment, supporting their mevalonate-pathway function, but in human skin rather than mouse hepatocytes.

evidence_span.text: Squalene synthase (SQS) utilizes FPP in the first committed step from the mevalonate pathway toward cholesterol biosynthesis.

reviews.rationale: This study directly pharmacologically characterizes squalene synthase (Fdft1) converting FPP to squalene in HepG2 hepatoma cells; Fdps is only mentioned as established background about NBP action, not newly investigated here.

evidence_span.text: Dual inhibition of ACLY and ACSS2 broke this cycle by reducing hepatic acetyl-CoA flux, suppressing DNL

reviews.rationale: Hepatic Acly knockdown activates the Acss2-acetyl-CoA pathway sustaining lipogenesis in a mouse NAFLD model, and dual Acss2+Acly inhibition was required to suppress hepatic DNL, directly matching the mechanism's claim.
